title: Reading Drill — Studying skate park use — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying skate park use — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on users waiting rather than sharing the narrowest ramp had already produced a small collection of timed observations. The park designer used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: wait time before each turn.

**B** The group kept a one-way entry pattern for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that group lessons should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
